preparation_note:
# Fresh recovery branch prepared 2026-10-26

This directory contains a new worker, native backend copy, recovery policy copy, and CPU-only preflight checks. The 2026-10-25 source branch is unchanged. No source corpus, tokenizer/model files, prior adapter, prior checkpoint, final/locked test fixture, or Drive/MCP artifact was read or modified during preparation.

The worker reads `hard_deadline_unix` and positive owner-authorized `reserve_seconds` from the scope file to derive the train cutoff; the current authorized values are 2026-10-26T11:14:18Z and 1500 seconds, yielding 10:49:18Z. The worker must be pointed at a separately staged trusted root after independent review. That root must supply its own current source/manifest, trusted renderer and inference contract, owner scope/deadline, and the preexisting 30-item development set already used by the earlier run; cached base outputs and prior adapter outputs are not acceptable. This is a reused development benchmark, not unseen or independent evaluation. Source QA remains required against the exact new plan and renderer before optimizer setup. The worker rejects inherited checkpoint resume and requires a fresh base.

The backend fetches the exact pinned model commit using `snapshot_download` with an allowlist built from the pinned weight index and known tokenizer/config metadata, verifies the commit snapshot and shards, then loads locally only. The worker checks the authorized cutoff before and after download/load. The prepared change uses LoRA r=16/alpha=16 over q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections, 2e-5 peak LR with 10-update linear warmup, microbatch 2/effective batch 16, non-reentrant gradient checkpointing, and 8-bit AdamW. Its explicit objective selects supervised shifted target logits only, computes CE on those positions, and gives equal weight to each row after averaging its assistant-token CE. Ignored prompt/padding positions are never passed to CE. The forward pass excludes labels so Transformers does not build an unused global-token loss graph; a first-microbatch selected-token reference checks value agreement, and CPU preflight checks values and gradients against a per-row loop. It preserves one-pass sampling, caps at 300 updates, pauses at 100 and 300, and also gates at end-of-view. This increases adaptation capacity and LR versus the prior weak 3e-6/r8 setting, so regression risk is higher; the paired development gate and retain-base selection policy remain mandatory. This is a training hypothesis, not a performance guarantee.

Preparation does not connect to MCP/T4, inspect or stage the source corpus, run training, or evaluate locked/final tests. A root-level reviewer must check this package and the later staged root before any run is launched.
